note: Rewritten from Thakur & Thakur 1992; original in English; the OCR has several mis-spellings and broken lines, and the measurements have been checked against the text and Table 29; the unit mm is as marked in the original. The original lists the species as Bulbitermes gedeensis (Kemner).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish brown, paler posteriorly, the tip of the nasus darker; antennae and pronotum pale brown; legs yellowish white, abdominal tergites brown with a dark brown tinge; head and body sparsely hairy. Body length (with nasus) about 3.40—4.10 mm. Posterior part of the head capsule wider and thicker, nasus rather long; outline weakly concave in dorsal view; slightly longer than wide (head length without nasus 1.05—1.10 mm, maximum head width 0.98—1.00 mm); posterior margin broadly rounded. Nasus cylindrical, without a basal swelling, nearly half the head capsule in length, nasus-head index 0.46—0.50. Antennae usually 13-segmented, occasionally 14; with 14 segments segment 3 is nearly as long as segment 2 and slightly shorter than segment 4; with 13 segments segment 3 is more than twice as long as segment 2 and 1.5 times as long as segment 4. Frontal gland and frontal tube distinct. Labrum small, wider than long, anterior margin weakly concave, anterior lateral corners rounded. Anteclypeus whitish, much wider than long; postclypeus distinct, anterior margin convex, posterior boundary not sharp. Apex of the right mandible with one distinct tooth. Postmentum wider than long (minimum median length 0.28 mm, maximum width 0.33 mm), widest in the middle, anterior margin nearly straight, posterior margin concave. Pronotum saddle-shaped, nearly twice as wide as long (maximum length 0.23—0.30 mm, width 0.50—0.55 mm), anterior and posterior margins both with a median notch. Mesonotum and metanotum convex posteriorly, without a median notch. Legs of moderate length, femora with many short hairs, tibiae more densely hairy; hind femur longer than the hind tibia.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The material is 4 soldiers and 3 workers from Panaitan Island (Sunda Strait, Indonesia), collected by Takuya Abe on 19 October 1982 (month 10, day 19). The original forms part of "Termites of the Krakatau Islands and adjacent islands", and the species is treated there as a new distribution record for Indonesia (it was previously recorded from Java).
